question: According to the Ember think tank, the EU upped its production of electricity from fossil fuels by 7 % in the first half of 2025 – to 368.46 TWh from 343.28 TWh in 2024 – resulting in a 5 % increase in power sector emissions, despite electricity demand only having grown by 0.7 %. This increase stems from the increased use of gas to compensate for the fall in wind production (-8.
5 %, -21 TWh) and hydropower production (-17 %, -33 TWh)1. This development is at odds with the European Green Deal’s climate and decarbonisation objectives2.

It lays bare the limits of an energy policy based on intermittent sources and the corresponding risks – which became apparent during Spain’s blackout in April 20253 – to the detriment of dispatchable capacities, in particular stored nuclear and hydraulic energy. 1.
How does the Commission explain this contradiction with its commitments to reduce emissions4 and increase use of renewable energy5?
Does it intend to shift the balance of EU energy policy in favour of stable and dispatchable sources to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and strengthen our energy security?

Contexte, Tuesday 7 October 2025. answer: Since the questions posed by the Honourable Member are actually addressed to the Commission, the Honourable Member is invited to send those questions to the Commission.
